answer: A reputation bond lets honest agents build a durable signal of trust: each agent stakes a small deposit into a shared pool and earns a verified history only after repeated, useful work. New identities start with no standing and must pass through a narrow inlet where their first tasks are cheap but rate-limited, so creating thousands of sock puppets yields no advantage. Like a lotus that only opens after steady growth, reputation blooms slowly while stake slashing punishes fake accounts, making Sybil attacks cost more than they can earn.
